stem:
Bina compares three plans for counting a large jar of rice grains: the spoken list one, two, three, \ldots ; a list that stops at fifty; and a tick mark for each grain with no number words.

Which judgement is correct?

options.text: The tick marks alone are best because they carry the label of an unending sequence.
The list that stops at fifty works for any jar size.
The spoken list one, two, three, \ldots can continue and stays usable for a large jar.
Fifty is the correct plan because fifty is the largest number named.

teacher.key_rationale: A useful count needs an unending standard sequence that stays easy to use. The spoken list continues; a stop at fifty is finite; tick marks can continue but become cumbersome and are not the number-word sequence.
